title: Systematic Literature Review on AI's Impact on Environmental Sustainability
author: Noemi Luna Carmeno

steps.title: Define Search Strings and Databases
steps.instruction: Develop specific search strings for two thematic groups (environment and human well-being) and adapt them to the syntax of Scopus, arXiv, and NBER working papers (via Google Scholar indexing).

substeps.instruction: For Scopus (Environmental): Use TITLE-ABS-KEY ( ( impact* OR footprint* OR effect) W/3 ( ai OR "Artificial Intelligence" OR ml OR "Machine Learning" OR "Deep Learning" OR llm* OR "Large Language Model*" ) W/3 ( environment* OR sustainab* OR ecological OR biodiversity OR carbon OR "climate change" OR energy OR resource* ) ) AND PUBYEAR > 2009 AND PUBYEAR < 2025 AND ( LIMIT-TO ( LANGUAGE,"English")).

For arXiv (Environmental): Use date_range: 2010-01-01 to 2024-12-31; AND title=ai OR "Artificial Intelligence" OR ml OR "Machine Learning" OR "Deep Learning" OR llm OR "Large Language Model"; AND abstract=environment OR environmental OR sustainable OR sustainability OR ecological OR biodiversity OR carbon OR "climate change" OR energy OR resources; AND abstract=impact OR footprint.

For arXiv (Human well-being): Use date_range: 2010-01-01 to 2024-12-31; AND title=ai OR "Artificial Intelligence" OR ml OR "Machine Learning" OR "Deep Learning" OR llm OR "Large Language Model"; AND abstract=wellbeing OR well-being OR happiness OR health OR employment OR unemployment OR labor OR labour OR job OR equality OR inequality OR society; AND abstract=impact OR implication.

For NBER (Environmental): Use site:nber.org (intitle:(ai OR "Artificial Intelligence" OR ml OR "Machine Learning" OR "Deep Learning" OR llm OR "Large Language Model" )) AND ( impact OR footprint OR effect ) AND ( environment OR environmental OR sustainable OR sustainability OR ecological OR biodiversity OR carbon OR "climate change" OR energy OR resources ) for dates 2010-2024.

For NBER (Human well-being): Use site:nber.org (intitle:(ai OR "Artificial Intelligence" OR ml OR "Machine Learning" OR "Deep Learning" OR llm OR "Large Language Model")) AND ( impact OR effect OR implications) AND ( wellbeing OR well-being OR happiness OR health OR employment OR unemployment OR labor OR labour OR job OR equality OR inequality OR society ) for dates 2010-2024.

steps.title: Execute Search and Identify Studies
steps.instruction: Perform the initial database searches and expand the results using citation tracking.

substeps.instruction: Conduct initial searches in Scopus, arXiv, and NBER working papers.
Perform backward citation tracking by screening the reference lists of included papers.
Perform forward citation tracking by identifying subsequent studies that cite the included papers.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Filter retrieved references based on specific inclusion criteria and quality assessments.

substeps.instruction: Apply inclusion criteria: Published on or after 2010, peer-reviewed articles, conference proceedings, working papers, preprints, or grey literature from reputable institutions, in English, with full text available and relevance to research questions.

Assess risk of bias at the study level during full-text screening using a quality checklist (data support, causal links, assumptions disclosure, proxies and measurements validation, circular reasoning, selective reporting).
Exclude studies classified as at critical risk of bias and record reasons in the PRISMA Flow Diagram.
Ensure overall review quality via the PRISMA 2020 framework, checklist, and guidelines.

steps.title: Extract Data from Studies
steps.instruction: Extract information into a structured Excel spreadsheet divided into three sections: bibliographic info/summary, categorized data (drop-downs/checkboxes), and open-text fields (findings, methods, limitations, gaps).

substeps.instruction: For 'very relevant' and 'relevant' studies, perform data extraction manually.
For 'less relevant' studies, use Microsoft 365 Copilot Enterprise with two iteratively developed standardized prompts.
Verify every piece of LLM-extracted information against the original text using a quality control checklist.
Perform spot checks on category tags on a random subset of records against source PDFs.

steps.title: Categorize Extracted Data
steps.instruction: Code the studies according to the following predefined categories:

substeps.instruction: Research line: AI environmental impact, AI well-being impact (cross-code if both).
Scale of analysis: macro (global, cross-country), macro (national, sub-national), micro (enterprise; set of projects/models), or micro (application/model/hardware).
Broad method: conceptual/theoretical, qualitative, or quantitative (categorize by predominant method).

Specific method: (Conceptual: Framework, Scoping/Lit Review, System Design, Ethical, Policy, Perspective); (Qualitative: Experimental Evaluation, Interview, Survey, Case Study, Participatory, Thematic/Content Analysis, Expert Elicitation); (Quantitative: Experimental Evaluation, Survey, Case Study, Statistical, Macroeconomic, LCA, Optimisation, Remote Sensing).

Impact type: (Environmental: energy, material, water, land use, ecological footprint, CO2, pollutants, biodiversity, SDGs); (Well-being: income, employment, inequality, health, subjective well-being, cognitive capabilities, social cohesion, existential risk).
Level of impact: computing-related, application-level (improvements in firms' performance or other), or systemic (rebound effects, shifts in consumer behaviour, or other).
Sentiment: positive, negative, or neutral based on authors' assessment or overall trend in abstract/discussion.

steps.title: Perform Analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct quantitative and qualitative analysis to synthesize findings.

substeps.instruction: Quantitative analysis: Map distribution across categories (research line, scale, method, impact type, level, sentiment) to highlight focus and identify gaps.
Qualitative analysis: Identify recurring/emerging findings and 'key findings' (high impact severity and confidence), and determine priorities for future work.

description: Author/s, Title, Year, Journal, Link, and Abstract of retrieved studies were downloaded in a spreadsheet. A second version of the spreadsheet containing only the titles and abstracts of the studies was created for the authors to proceed with the title and abstract screening blind to authorship and publication source. Prior to first screening, duplicates were removed. After first screening, full-text studies were checked for eligibility, providing inclusion/ exclusion reasons and explanations in the PRISMA Flow Diagram. Available and eligible studies were included in the review and classified by relevance to the research questions into three categories: very relevant (the study’s core contribution directly addresses one or more research questions), relevant (the study addresses one or more research questions, but this is not its core contribution), and less relevant (the study tangentially addresses or intersects with one or more research questions). Title, abstract, and keywords Outputs of data extraction were: study summary to get an overview of the studies’ content; categorisation of the publications into research line, scale of analysis, broad method, specific method, impact type, level at which impacts arise, and sentiment categories; identification of the key findings of the study; identification of the methods employed by the study and associated limitations; identification of the main research gaps highlighted by the study.
